meta.title: Tamil Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 38 letters and signs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Tamil script: 38 notes, in the traditional order — the twelve vowels, the āytam (ஃ) and the puḷḷi (the dot that silences a consonant's vowel), the eighteen consonants in the order Tamil primers teach them, and the six Grantha letters borrowed for words from Sanskrit and English (ஜ, ஷ, ஸ, ஹ, க்ஷ, ஸ்ரீ). The first deck of the Tamil collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Each vowel is shown alone and as the sign it becomes after a consonant, written on க (ஆ · கா), since the sign is what a reader meets most: every one of the 216 consonant-vowel letters is one of those signs on one of these consonants. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them. Tamil script writes no difference between k and g, t and d, or p and b — one letter is said one way at the start of a word and another between vowels — and it has three n's, three l's and two r's that English does not tell apart; where English has no equivalent, the card says what to do with the tongue instead. Sources: the standard description of modern standard Tamil; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: அ
fields.Sound: a · a short "a", like the u of cup or the a of about; every consonant carries it unless a sign or the puḷḷi says otherwise, so it has no sign of its own

fields.Name: ஆ
fields.Sound: ā · "a" as in father, long

fields.Name: இ
fields.Sound: i · "i" as in bit, short

fields.Name: ஈ
fields.Sound: ī · "ee" as in see, long

fields.Name: உ
fields.Sound: u · "u" as in put, short; at the end of a word often said with the lips unrounded, almost swallowed. Its sign changes shape from consonant to consonant (கு, டு, மு), so each is learnt by sight

fields.Name: ஊ
fields.Sound: ū · "oo" as in food, long; its sign too changes shape with the consonant

fields.Name: எ
fields.Sound: e · "e" as in bed, short; its sign is written BEFORE the consonant it follows in speech

fields.Name: ஏ
fields.Sound: ē · like the a of cake held long, one pure vowel without the glide into "ee"; its sign too is written before the consonant

fields.Name: ஐ
fields.Sound: ai · "ai" as in aisle; its sign is written before the consonant

fields.Name: ஒ
fields.Sound: o · a short pure "o", between the o of hot and the o of go; its sign is written around the consonant, one part before it and one after

fields.Name: ஓ
fields.Sound: ō · like the o of go held long, one pure vowel without the glide into "oo"; its sign too is written around the consonant

fields.Name: ஔ
fields.Sound: au · "ow" as in cow; the rarest vowel, its sign written around the consonant
fields.Example: ஔவைauvaielderly woman; the name of the poet Auvaiyar

fields.Name: ஆய்தம்
fields.Sound: ḥ · āytam, the three dots: a rare sign, a soft breath of "h" in a few old words; before ப it writes the f of English words (ஃப = f)

fields.Name: புள்ளி
fields.Sound: puḷḷi, the dot above: the consonant has NO vowel after it (க் = k); a consonant without it carries a (க = ka)

fields.Name: க
fields.Sound: ka · "k" at the start of a word and when doubled (க்க); a "g" after ங (ங்க); between vowels a soft g, often almost h (மகன் makaṉ, said "magan")

fields.Name: ங
fields.Sound: ṅa · "ng" as in sing; almost always just before க (ங்க), and never starts a word

fields.Name: ச
fields.Sound: ca · at the start of a word an "s" in most speech, or "ch"; "ch" when doubled (ச்ச); a "j" after ஞ (ஞ்ச); between vowels an "s"

fields.Name: ஞ
fields.Sound: ña · "ny" as in canyon; mostly before ச (ஞ்ச), and at the start of a few words

fields.Name: ட
fields.Sound: ṭa · a "t" with the tongue tip curled back to the roof of the mouth (retroflex); never starts a Tamil word; between vowels it becomes a curled-back "d" (வீடு vīṭu, said "veedu")

fields.Name: ண
fields.Sound: ṇa · an "n" with the tongue tip curled back (retroflex); never starts a word

fields.Name: த
fields.Sound: ta · a soft "t" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental), as in French or Spanish; between vowels a soft dental "d", near the th of this

fields.Name: ந
fields.Sound: na · an "n" with the tongue against the upper teeth (dental); the n that starts a word, and the one before த (ந்த)

fields.Name: ப
fields.Sound: pa · "p" at the start of a word and when doubled (ப்ப); a "b" after ம (ம்ப) and, softly, between vowels

fields.Name: ம
fields.Sound: ma · "m" as in man

fields.Name: ய
fields.Sound: ya · "y" as in yes

fields.Name: ர
fields.Sound: ra · a single tap of the tongue, like the r of Spanish pero; never starts a Tamil word (the English "rail" is written இரயில், with a vowel first)

fields.Name: ல
fields.Sound: la · "l" as in leaf, the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth

fields.Name: வ
fields.Sound: va · between "v" and "w": the lower lip only lightly touches the teeth

fields.Name: ழ
fields.Sound: ḻa · the sound Tamil is known for: the tongue tip curled far back and held without touching the roof of the mouth, near an American r said with the tongue turned up; often written zh in English (Tamizh)

fields.Name: ள
fields.Sound: ḷa · an "l" with the tongue tip curled back to the roof of the mouth (retroflex)

fields.Name: ற
fields.Sound: ṟa · a firmer r than ர, tapped or trilled further forward; doubled (ற்ற) it is said "ttr", or as a hard t; never starts a word

fields.Name: ன
fields.Sound: ṉa · an "n" as in English, the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth (alveolar); never starts a word, and ends very many

fields.Name: ஜ
fields.Sound: ja · "j" as in jam — a Grantha letter, borrowed for words from Sanskrit and English

fields.Name: ஷ
fields.Sound: ṣa · "sh" as in ship — a Grantha letter

fields.Name: ஸ
fields.Sound: sa · "s" as in sun — a Grantha letter

fields.Name: ஹ
fields.Sound: ha · "h" as in hand — a Grantha letter

fields.Name: க்ஷ
fields.Sound: kṣa · a joined Grantha letter, க் + ஷ, said "ksh"

fields.Name: ஸ்ரீ
fields.Sound: śrī · a joined Grantha letter, ஸ் + ர + ீ, said "shree" or "sree": the honorific Sri, written as one shape
